common_name: Sanguinea Rose (Bengal Crimson, Deep Blood-Red China Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; Sanguinea, also called Bengal Crimson, is a China rose bearing single, deep blood-red flowers on a tough, nearly evergreen shrub in the mildest climates.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, compost-enriched soil. Sanguinea, also widely known as Bengal Crimson, bears simple, single, velvety deep blood-red flowers with a light fragrance, opening almost continuously through the warm season on a vigorous, nearly evergreen shrub in mild winter climates. Its intense, saturated color and open flower form make it a striking accent among the many pastel-toned old garden roses, and it draws pollinators readily thanks to its accessible single blooms. Like other China roses it shows excellent resistance to blackspot and powdery mildew in humid conditions and blooms reliably with minimal spray intervention. Prune lightly in late winter to remove dead or crossing wood; it reblooms readily even without deadheading.

common_name: Green Rose (Novelty China Rose with Petal-Like Green Sepals)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; the Green Rose is a botanical novelty in which the petals are replaced by leaf-like green bracts, so it never produces a conventional colorful flower.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, compost-enriched soil. The Green Rose is one of the most unusual novelty roses in cultivation, a natural mutation of a China rose in which the normal petals are entirely replaced by small, ruffled, leaf-like green bracts, so the plant never produces conventional colored petals and has essentially no fragrance. Grown for curiosity and conversation value more than for a traditional floral display, it flowers nearly continuously through the warm season on a compact, well-branched China-type shrub and makes an unusual, long-lasting cut flower that dries well. Like other China roses it shows good resistance to blackspot and powdery mildew and requires minimal spray intervention. Prune lightly in late winter to shape and remove dead or crossing wood.

common_name: Comtesse du Cayla Rose (Coppery Orange-Pink Antique China Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; Comtesse du Cayla, introduced in 1902, is a China rose noted for its unusual coppery orange-pink flower color and reddish new foliage.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, compost-enriched soil. Comtesse du Cayla, introduced in France in 1902, bears loosely double, semi-double flowers in an unusual warm blend of coppery-orange, salmon, and pink that shifts tone as the blooms age, with a light, fruity fragrance and reddish-tinted new growth that adds further color interest. It flowers nearly continuously through the warm season on a compact, well-branched shrub typical of the China class. Like other China roses it shows excellent resistance to blackspot and powdery mildew in humid conditions, blooming reliably with little spray intervention. Prune lightly in late winter to remove dead or crossing wood; it reblooms readily even without deadheading.

common_name: Papa Gontier Rose (Antique Pink-and-Red Tea Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; Papa Gontier, introduced in 1883, is a classic antique tea rose long grown in Southern gardens for its elegant pointed buds and reliable performance in poor soil.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil. Papa Gontier, introduced in France in 1883, bears long, elegant, pointed buds in deep rose-pink with a carmine-red reverse, opening to loosely double, fragrant flowers prized in the 19th century as a cut flower and boutonniere rose for its refined bud shape. Like other old tea roses it flowers nearly continuously from spring to frost, tolerates poor, sandy soil far better than modern hybrid teas, and shows good resistance to blackspot in humid Gulf South conditions. Long grown in Southern homestead and cemetery plantings with little care, it needs only light pruning in late winter to remove dead or crossing wood and control size.
